correctness.rationale: The bipartite-class dichotomy reduces all candidate equalizers to two cases. The larger class B itself works for q>=3. For A-containing sets, if at least two depth-one vertices u_i are omitted, each corresponding leaf w_i must be selected because u_i is the unique midpoint of a four-edge cross-arm pair; otherwise at least q-1 depth-one vertices are already selected. This gives the sharp 2q lower bound. Equality forces either B or A plus all but one u_i, and each such set is checked explicitly. The direct checker exhaustively confirms all subsets through the target size for q=3..6.

value.rationale: The foundational literature explicitly leaves exact equidistant dimension of trees as a natural open direction. Balanced three-edge spiders are a canonical symmetric infinite tree family, not an arbitrary finite slice. The result gives the exact parameter and every minimum set, and shows an unbounded q-1 gap beyond the generic bipartite side-size lower bound. The cross-arm midpoint mechanism is structural and suggests extensions to broader spider families.
